title: DHS OIG: ICE's Immigration Surge Caused 39% Drop in HSI Fentanyl Seizures, 31% Decline in Investigation Hours
excerpt: A DHS OIG audit published August 22, 2026 (OIG-26-23) found that ICE Homeland Security Investigations' fentanyl seizures fell 39 percent in fiscal year 2025 as the agency shifted agents to immigration enforcement operations, and that investigative hours dedicated to fentanyl declined by more than 250,000 hours — approximately 31 percent — compared to the prior year.
content:
DHS OIG report OIG-26-23, published August 22, 2026, examined how ICE Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) countered fentanyl entering the United States during fiscal years 2024–2025. Three government shutdowns in FY 2026 significantly delayed publication of the audit.

  • As ICE shifted priorities toward immigration enforcement, HSI agents reported an "all hands-on deck" environment beginning in January 2025, with fentanyl investigations declining sharply as a result.
  • Fentanyl seizures decreased by approximately 39 percent in fiscal year 2025; investigative hours dedicated to fentanyl countering declined by more than 250,000 hours, or about 31 percent, compared to fiscal year 2024.
  • The report found HSI technology used during fentanyl investigations had significant limitations, and agents were hindered by delays in obtaining funds to purchase evidence, a lack of independent Title 21 authority, and low referral rates of fentanyl cases from CBP.

The OIG made four recommendations, including that HSI review staffing levels to ensure appropriate coverage for fentanyl investigations. ICE concurred with all four recommendations and estimated completion by June 2027. The Attorney General's office separately issued a memorandum in May 2026 granting HSI Title 21 authority to assist DOJ in enforcing the Controlled Substances Act — partially addressing one of the audit's concerns.
source: DHS Office of Inspector General / WTOP News
